subject: english
question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

He worked very **hardly** to pass the exam.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word "**hardly**" is incorrect in the given context. "Hardly" means "barely" or "almost not," which does not fit the intended meaning of the sentence.
 
• The correct word to use is "**hard**," which means "with a lot of effort" and accurately conveys the idea.
 
• Thus, replacing "hardly" with "hard" improves the clarity and correctness of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 3**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"He worked very hard to pass the exam."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "sincerely" **– While "sincerely" conveys a sense of genuine effort, it does not accurately describe the intensity of effort required to pass an exam.
 
• **Option 2: "regularly" **– This implies consistency but does not convey the idea of working with great effort.
 
• **Option 4: "harder" **– This is a comparative term and would not fit in the context without specifying what is being compared.
